correctness.rationale: The standard simplex integral equals the divided difference of the exponential at the five vertex-phase nodes. At distinct integer nodes, all exponential values equal one and the fourth divided difference of a constant is zero. At repeated nodes, the exact confluent-residue formula is a polynomial over the rationals in \(i/(2\pi)\); transcendence of \(\pi\) means only the zero polynomial can vanish. A unique maximal multiplicity yields a nonzero lowest coefficient. The only tied maximum is the two-endpoints-plus-singleton pattern, whose lowest coefficient vanishes exactly at the midpoint; direct residues then sum to zero. The proof covers every integer frequency. The included checker verifies 210 bounded multisets exactly, without treating finite enumeration as the proof.
